t: The Nubians are indigenous to the Nile valley between southern Egypt and northern Sudan, where Neolithic settlements date back to 7000 BC, and they speak Nilo-Saharan Nubian languages with Arabic as a second language.
Nubia was home to the Kerma culture, the Kingdom of Kush and the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, under which all of Egypt was united with Nubia from 744 to 656 BC.
The Aswan High Dam, built from the 1960s, flooded much of Lower Nubia and displaced 100,000 Nubians, many of them forcibly relocated to New Halfa, Khashm el Girba and “New Nubia” near Kom Ombo.
dyk: During the Yom Kippur War of 1973, Egypt used Nubians as code talkers.
ev: Neolithic settlements appear in central Nubia, with Wadi Halfa believed to be the oldest settlement of the central Nile valley
The Twenty-fifth Dynasty unites all of Egypt with Nubia
Eratosthenes records the Noubai west of the Nile as a numerous people divided into several kingdoms
The Kingdom of Kush disintegrates and gives way to Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia
Makuria repulses the Rashidun Caliphate’s invasion and the Baqt treaty is signed
Old Nubian is first attested in writing
Most Nubians have converted to Islam
The Aswan High Dam floods much of Lower Nubia and displaces about 100,000 Nubians

f.homeland: Nubia, from southern Egypt to northern Sudan; today Aswan Governorate in Egypt, especially Kom Ombo and Nasr al-Nuba, and Sudan’s Northern State from Wadi Halfa to al Dabbah near the Fourth Cataract, with many in Cairo and Khartoum; also the Midob and Birgid of Darfur and the Hill Nubians of Kordofan; ancient centres Kerma, Napata, Jebel Barkal and Meroë
f.period: Neolithic settlements from 7000 BC; the A-Group (3700–2800 BC), C-Group (2300–1600 BC) and Kerma (2500–1500 BC) cultures; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty (744–656 BC); Napata and Meroë (to 300/350 AD); the Christian kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria and Alodia (4th century to 1504); Islamization by the 16th century; displacement by the Aswan High Dam from the 1960s
f.known: the Nubian languages, among them Nobiin and Old Nubian, written from the 8th century AD; archers famed in antiquity (“Land of the Bow”); the Twenty-fifth Dynasty that ruled all of Egypt; the pyramids of Jebel Barkal, Nuri, El Kerru and Meroë; the frescoes of Faras; the Baqt treaty; the Nubian vault; the Sebu birth ceremony
f.sources: Egyptian texts, Greek authors such as Eratosthenes preserved in Strabo, Meroitic inscriptions and Greek inscriptions such as Silko’s at Kalabsha; Old Nubian documents; archaeology from Qustul to Kulubnarti; linguistic work by Claude Rilly, Julien Cooper and others; genetic studies of ancient and living Nubians
